CSCO.rationale: Cisco's stock has experienced a massive +62.5% quarterly surge, pushing the P/E to 46.8x — nearly double the 26.2x low from a year ago and at the absolute top of its 365-day range. This extreme valuation expansion has occurred despite fundamental headwinds: gross margins are compressing (66.0% non-GAAP vs 68.6% YoY, driven by memory costs and tariffs), operating cash flow declined 43.3% QoQ and 18.7% YoY, and the security/observability segment (including Splunk) remains flat. The RPO growth of 5% YoY lags the 10% revenue growth, suggesting the AI hardware boom is not converting into durable recurring revenue. While Q3 results beat estimates and guidance was raised, the stock has already priced in far more than the fundamental improvement — the P/E has nearly doubled while EPS grew ~31% YoY. The GF Score flags valuation at 1/10, and multiple sources describe the stock as significantly overvalued. With the next earnings not until August 12, there is no near-term catalyst to sustain this stretched multiple, and the risk of mean reversion in valuation is substantial.
